# Welcome

This is Part 2 of the analysis for the paper *"Knowledge Gaps and Sequencing Priorities for Mammalian eDNA Metabarcoding in the World's Largest Tropical Forest Country"*. It uses the reference sequences and species data prepared in `1_Prepare_data.Rmd`.

In this document, we assess reference database completeness across primers and taxonomic orders, sequence ambiguity (identical sequences shared between species), sequence divergence, the depth of coverage (number of distinct sequences per species), and the complementarity between primers.

**Input:** `output/intermediate/1_Prepare_data.rds` (Part 1).

**Output:** `output/intermediate/2_Assess_completeness_ambiguity_complementarity.rds`, used by Part 3; Figures 1 and 2 and the related supplementary figures and tables.

**Plotting helper:**

Since gghalves is no longer maintained, we manually create half-violins with standard ggplot2 layers.

```{r}

# Polygons for half-violins: for each level of the factor `x`, a kernel
# density of `y` drawn to the right of the level's position, scaled to a
# common maximum width.

half_violin_polygons <- function(data, x, y, width = 0.45) {
  groups <- split(as.data.frame(data), data[[x]], drop = TRUE)
  do.call(rbind, lapply(groups, function(d) {
    values <- d[[y]]
    if (length(unique(values)) < 2) return(NULL)
    dens <- stats::density(values)
    pos  <- as.integer(d[[x]][1])
    data.frame(
      group  = pos,
      region = d$region[1],
      x      = c(pos, pos + dens$y / max(dens$y) * width, pos),
      y      = c(min(dens$x), dens$x, max(dens$x))
    )
  }))
}

```

# 1. Database completeness

## 1.1. Presence of Brazilian species in the reference databases

First, we will check whether any of our Brazilian mammals species or their synonyms are present in the reference database, and if so, how many unique sequences we have in the database per species.

We will create a data frame that contains both the presence/absence data of Brazilian mammal species, as well as unique sequence counts, for each reference databases (amplicon region/primer pair combination).

We will do this for two sets of the data:

1.  All sequences: species with at least one sequence in the database, regardless of whether that sequence is shared with other species.
2.  Unambiguous sequences: species with at least one sequence that is not shared with any other species in the checklist. Sequence ambiguity is assessed within the Brazilian mammal checklist. A species with several sequences, of which some are shared with other species and some are not, is counted as present for unambiguous sequences, because it retains at least one unambiguous sequence.

In the code, the unambiguous sets are labelled `unique`.

**For each species and its synonyms, check the presence and number of unique sequences in the eDNA dataframe for each region/primer combination:**

```{r}
# 2. Analyzing database completeness

# Assess presence of Brazilian mammal species in the reference eDNA database.
# We check for both:

#   1) All detected sequences per species (including sequences shared across species)

#   2) Unique sequences per species (sequences not shared with other species)

# 2.1. Prepare list to store detected sequences for all species, for each region/primer

brz_mam_sequences_all <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_eDNA))
names(brz_mam_sequences_all) <- names(brz_mam_eDNA)

for (i in seq_along(brz_mam_sequences_all)) {
  
  # Prepare a list to store sequences per species (including synonyms)
  brz_mam_sequences_all[[i]] <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_synonyms))
  names(brz_mam_sequences_all[[i]]) <- names(brz_mam_synonyms)
  
  for (j in seq_along(brz_mam_synonyms)) {
    
    # Subset eDNA sequences that match the species or its synonyms
    subset <- brz_mam_eDNA[[i]][names(brz_mam_eDNA[[i]]) %in% brz_mam_synonyms[[j]]]
    
    # Extract first sequence for each entry
    subset <- sapply(subset, function(x) x[1])
    
    # If sequences exist, convert to a data.frame, else fill with NA
    if (length(subset) > 0) {
      subset <- data.frame(
        binomial = names(brz_mam_synonyms)[j],
        sequence = unlist(subset)
      )
      subset <- unique(subset)  # Remove duplicate sequences
    } else {
      subset <- data.frame(
        binomial = names(brz_mam_synonyms)[j],
        sequence = NA
      )
    }
    
    # Extract region and primer information from the list name
    subset$region <- stringr::str_split(names(brz_mam_sequences_all)[i], pattern = "_")[[1]][1]
    subset$primer <- paste(
      stringr::str_split(names(brz_mam_sequences_all)[i], pattern = "_")[[1]][-1],
      collapse = "_"
    )
    
    # Store results
    brz_mam_sequences_all[[i]][[j]] <- subset
  }
  
  # Combine all species for this region/primer into a single data.frame
  brz_mam_sequences_all[[i]] <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_sequences_all[[i]])
}

# 2.2. Detect sequences that are unique to each species

# For sequences shared across multiple species, set to NA

brz_mam_sequences_unique <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_all))

for (i in seq_along(brz_mam_sequences_all)) {
  brz_mam_sequences_unique[[i]] <- brz_mam_sequences_all[[i]] %>%
    group_by(sequence) %>%
    mutate(sequence = ifelse(n_distinct(binomial) > 1, NA, sequence)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# 2.3. Summarize completeness and sequence depth for all detected sequences

# For each species, calculate:

#   - nseq: number of distinct sequences
#   - presence: 1 if >=1 sequence, 0 if none

brz_mam_completeness_all <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_all))
names(brz_mam_completeness_all) <- names(brz_mam_sequences_all)

for (i in seq_along(brz_mam_sequences_all)) {
  brz_mam_completeness_all[[i]] <- brz_mam_sequences_all[[i]] %>%
    group_by(binomial) %>%
    summarize(
      nseq = n_distinct(sequence, na.rm = TRUE),
      region = first(region),
      primer = first(primer)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Replace NA sequence counts with 0 and create presence column
  brz_mam_completeness_all[[i]]$nseq[is.na(brz_mam_completeness_all[[i]]$nseq)] <- 0
  brz_mam_completeness_all[[i]]$presence <- ifelse(brz_mam_completeness_all[[i]]$nseq > 0, 1, 0)
  
  brz_mam_completeness_all[[i]] <- brz_mam_completeness_all[[i]] %>%
    relocate(binomial, nseq, presence)
}

# 2.4. Summarize completeness for uniquely detected sequences
brz_mam_completeness_unique <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_unique))
names(brz_mam_completeness_unique) <- names(brz_mam_sequences_unique)

for (i in seq_along(brz_mam_sequences_unique)) {
  brz_mam_completeness_unique[[i]] <- brz_mam_sequences_unique[[i]] %>%
    group_by(binomial) %>%
    summarize(
      nseq = n_distinct(sequence, na.rm = TRUE),
      region = first(region),
      primer = first(primer)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  brz_mam_completeness_unique[[i]]$nseq[is.na(brz_mam_completeness_unique[[i]]$nseq)] <- 0
  brz_mam_completeness_unique[[i]]$presence <- ifelse(brz_mam_completeness_unique[[i]]$nseq > 0, 1, 0)
  
  brz_mam_completeness_unique[[i]] <- brz_mam_completeness_unique[[i]] %>%
    relocate(binomial, nseq, presence)
}

# 2.5. Combine list elements into single data.frames for downstream analysis
brz_mam_sequences_all <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_sequences_all)
brz_mam_sequences_unique <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_sequences_unique)

brz_mam_completeness_all <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_completeness_all)
brz_mam_completeness_unique <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_completeness_unique)

# 2.6. Remove temporary objects
rm(subset, i, j)

```

## 1.2. Explore database completeness

### 1.2.1. ***Database completeness per primer***

Here, we calculate the percentage of Brazilian mammal species with at least one reference sequence for each primer, and, for species with reference sequences, how many distinct sequences are present (haplotypic depth).

**Prepare the data for plotting:**

```{r}

# 1. Aggregate completeness for all detected sequences

# For each region/primer, calculate percent of species with:

#   - 1 sequence
#   - 2–5 sequences
#   - 6–10 sequences
#   - >10 sequences

# Also calculate cumulative sequence count per primer for ordering purposes

brz_mam_primer_completeness_all <- brz_mam_completeness_all %>%
  
  # Remove species and presence columns, since we only need nseq, region, primer
  select(-c(binomial, presence)) %>%
  
  # Group by amplicon region and primer
  group_by(region, primer) %>%
  
  # Compute percentage of species in each nseq bin
  summarize(
    "1"    = (sum(nseq == 1) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100,
    "2-5"  = (sum(nseq > 1 & nseq < 6) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100,
    "6-10" = (sum(nseq > 5 & nseq < 11) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100,
    ">10"  = (sum(nseq > 10) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100
  ) %>%
  
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  
  # Convert wide-format nseq bins into long format for plotting or further analysis
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("1", "2-5", "6-10", ">10"),
    names_to = "nseqs",
    values_to = "seq_count"
  ) %>%
  
  # Compute cumulative sequence counts per primer
  group_by(primer) %>%
  mutate(cumsum = sum(seq_count)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


# 2. Repeat for uniquely detected sequences

# Same as above, but using the uniqueness-filtered dataset

brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique <- brz_mam_completeness_unique %>%
  select(-c(binomial, presence)) %>%
  group_by(region, primer) %>%
  summarize(
    "1"    = (sum(nseq == 1) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100,
    "2-5"  = (sum(nseq > 1 & nseq < 6) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100,
    "6-10" = (sum(nseq > 5 & nseq < 11) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100,
    ">10"  = (sum(nseq > 10) / length(brz_mam_synonyms)) * 100
  ) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("1", "2-5", "6-10", ">10"),
    names_to = "nseqs",
    values_to = "seq_count"
  ) %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  mutate(cumsum = sum(seq_count)) %>%
  dplyr::ungroup()


# 3. Factor levels for nseq bins

levels_nseqs <- c(">10", "6-10", "2-5", "1")

brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$nseqs    <- factor(brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$nseqs, levels = levels_nseqs)
brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$nseqs <- factor(brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$nseqs, levels = levels_nseqs)


# 4. Create region_nseqs labels for plotting

# Combines region and nseq bin for x-axis ordering

brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$region_nseqs    <- paste(brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$region, brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$nseqs, sep = "_")
brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$region_nseqs <- paste(brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$region, brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$nseqs, sep = "_")

levels_region_nseqs <- c(
  "12S_>10", "12S_6-10", "12S_2-5", "12S_1",
  "16S_>10", "16S_6-10", "16S_2-5", "16S_1",
  "COI_>10", "COI_6-10", "COI_2-5", "COI_1",
  "Cytb_>10", "Cytb_6-10", "Cytb_2-5", "Cytb_1"
)

brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$region_nseqs    <- factor(brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$region_nseqs, levels = levels_region_nseqs)
brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$region_nseqs <- factor(brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$region_nseqs, levels = levels_region_nseqs)


# 5. Reorder primers based on cumulative sequence counts

# Primers with higher total sequence coverage appear first

brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$primer    <- reorder(brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$primer, brz_mam_primer_completeness_all$cumsum, decreasing = TRUE)
brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$primer <- reorder(brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$primer, brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique$cumsum, decreasing = TRUE)

```

**Plot the data:**

```{r, fig.width=30, fig.height=7.5, fig.dpi= 600}

# 1. Define color palettes for each region

# Lighten base colors to create a gradient for different nseq bins

palette_1 <- colorspace::lighten(col = "#68a898", amount = seq(0.0, 0.5, length.out = 4))
palette_2 <- colorspace::lighten(col = "#b62c25", amount = seq(0.0, 0.5, length.out = 4))

  `16S_>10` = palette_2[1], `16S_6-10` = palette_2[2], `16S_2-5` = palette_2[3], `16S_1` = palette_2[4],
  `COI_>10` = palette_3[1], `COI_6-10` = palette_3[2], `COI_2-5` = palette_3[3], `COI_1` = palette_3[4],

)

# Custom labels for legend (showing only nseq bins)

custom_labels <- c(

  "16S_>10" = ">10", "16S_6-10" = "6-10", "16S_2-5" = "2-5", "16S_1" = "1",
  "COI_>10" = ">10", "COI_6-10" = "6-10", "COI_2-5" = "2-5", "COI_1" = "1",

# 2. Plot for all detected sequences

# Stacked barplot showing percentage of species with sequences per primer

primer_completeness_plot_all <- ggplot(brz_mam_primer_completeness_all) +
  
  # Stacked bars for each primer, colored by region_nseqs

# 3. Plot for uniquely detected sequences

primer_completeness_plot_unique <- ggplot(brz_mam_primer_completeness_unique) +
```

### 1.2.2. ***Database completeness per primer and order***

We look at the completeness and depth per primer for each taxonomic order. These plots are saved as supplementary figures (`completeness_by_primer_<Order>`).

**Prepare the data:**

```{r}

# 1. Count the number of species per clade (order)

# This creates a data frame with the total number of species in each mammalian order.

nspecies_per_clade <- 
  brz_mam_taxonomy %>%
  select(order) %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  mutate(n_species = n()) %>%  # Count species per order
  unique() %>%                 # Keep one row per order
  ungroup()


# 2. Quantify completeness per clade and primer (all sequences)

# For each order, region, and primer:

#   - Count number of species with 1, 2-5, 6-10, or >10 sequences
#   - Calculate percentage relative to total species in that order

brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all <- 
  merge(brz_mam_completeness_all, brz_mam_taxonomy, by = "binomial") %>%
  merge(., nspecies_per_clade, by = "order") %>%
  select(binomial, nseq, region, primer, order, n_species) %>%
  group_by(order, region, primer) %>%
  summarize(
    "1"     = sum(nseq == 1),
    "2-5"   = sum(nseq > 1 & nseq < 6),
    "6-10"  = sum(nseq > 5 & nseq < 11),
    ">10"   = sum(nseq > 10),
    n_species = unique(n_species)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("1", "2-5", "6-10", ">10"),
    names_to = "nseqs",
    values_to = "seq_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(seq_perc = (seq_count / n_species) * 100) %>%   # Percentage of species in clade
  group_by(order, region, primer) %>%
  mutate(cumsum = sum(seq_perc)) %>%                     # Cumulative completeness
  ungroup()


# 3. Repeat for unique sequences only

# Same as above but considering only unambiguous (unique) sequences.

brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_unique <- 
  merge(brz_mam_completeness_unique, brz_mam_taxonomy, by = "binomial") %>%
  merge(., nspecies_per_clade, by = "order") %>%
  select(binomial, nseq, region, primer, order, n_species) %>%
  group_by(order, region, primer) %>%
  summarize(
    "1"     = sum(nseq == 1),
    "2-5"   = sum(nseq > 1 & nseq < 6),
    "6-10"  = sum(nseq > 5 & nseq < 11),
    ">10"   = sum(nseq > 10),
    n_species = unique(n_species)
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("1", "2-5", "6-10", ">10"),
    names_to = "nseqs",
    values_to = "seq_count"
  ) %>%
  mutate(seq_perc = (seq_count / n_species) * 100) %>%
  group_by(order, region, primer) %>%
  mutate(cumsum = sum(seq_perc)) %>%
  ungroup()


# 4. Final fine-tuning: factor levels and combined identifiers

# Order nseqs for plotting, and create region_nseqs combining region and nseqs.

factor_levels <- c(">10", "6-10", "2-5", "1")

brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all$nseqs <- factor(
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all$nseqs,
  levels = factor_levels
)

brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_unique$nseqs <- factor(
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_unique$nseqs,
  levels = factor_levels
)

brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all$region_nseqs <- paste(
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all$region,
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all$nseqs,
  sep = "_"
)

brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_unique$region_nseqs <- paste(
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_unique$region,
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_unique$nseqs,
  sep = "_"
)

region_levels <- c(
  "12S_>10", "12S_6-10", "12S_2-5", "12S_1",
  "16S_>10", "16S_6-10", "16S_2-5", "16S_1",
  "COI_>10", "COI_6-10", "COI_2-5", "COI_1",
```

```{r, fig.width=28, fig.height=8, fig.dpi= 600}
# 2. Generate clade-level completeness plots (all sequences)

# Loop through each order and create a stacked bar plot showing the proportion
# of species with 1, 2-5, 6-10, or >10 sequences for each primer and region.
# Add phylopic icons 

clade_primer_completeness_plot_list_all <- vector("list")

orders <- unique(brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all$order)

for (i in seq_along(orders)) {
  
  order <- orders[i]
  
  # Subset data for current order
  data_all <- brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all %>%
    filter(order == !!order)
  
  # Reorder primers by cumulative completeness
  data_all$primer <- reorder(data_all$primer, data_all$cumsum, decreasing = TRUE)
  
  # Create plot
  clade_primer_completeness_plot_list_all[[i]] <- 
    ggplot(data_all) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.5, color = "grey80") +
    geom_bar(aes(x = primer, y = seq_perc, fill = region_nseqs),
             position = "stack", stat = "identity", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_text(aes(x = primer, y = cumsum, label = round(cumsum, 1)), vjust = -0.5, size = 8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = combined_palette, labels = custom_labels, name = "Number of unique barcodes") +
    scale_y_continuous(
      limits = c(0, ifelse(max(data_all$cumsum) * 1.7 > 100, max(data_all$cumsum) * 1.7, 110)),
      expand = c(0, 0),
      breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
      labels = function(x) ifelse(x <= 100, x, "")
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(labels = str_to_upper) +
    ylab("Species with barcode (%)") +
    xlab("Primers for different regions") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold", color = "black"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 22, color = "black"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 26, color = "black"),
      axis.title.x = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 30),
      legend.position = c(0.24, 0.85),
      legend.direction = "horizontal",
      legend.title.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 30, color = "black"),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 12, color = "black")
    ) +
    ggtitle("All sequences") +
    add_phylopic(
      img = phylopics[[order]],
      x = levels(data_all$primer)[length(levels(data_all$primer)) - 3],
      y = ifelse(max(data_all$cumsum) * 1.7 > 100, max(data_all$cumsum) * 1.7, 100) * 0.8,
      height = 20 * size_multiplier[i],
      alpha = 0.8,
      horizontal = mirror[i],
      fill = custom_colors[order]
    )
}
```

### 1.2.3. ***Database completeness at increasing depth***

Code for plotting Figure 1C.

**Prepare the data:**

```{r}

# 1. Compute completeness per depth for all sequences

brz_mam_primer_completeness_depth_all <- brz_mam_completeness_all %>%
  select(!c(binomial, presence)) %>%
  group_by(region, primer) %>%
  summarize(
    ">=1"  = sum(nseq >= 1)  / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100,
    ">=2"  = sum(nseq >= 2)  / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100,
    ">=5"  = sum(nseq >= 5)  / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100,
    ">=10" = sum(nseq >= 10) / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(">=1", ">=2", ">=5", ">=10"),
                      names_to = "nseqs",
                      values_to = "seq_count") %>%
  mutate(nseqs = factor(nseqs, levels = c(">=1", ">=2", ">=5", ">=10")))


# Mean values for annotation

mean_by_threshold <- brz_mam_primer_completeness_depth_all %>%
  group_by(nseqs) %>%
  summarize(mean_seq_count = mean(seq_count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_change = (mean_seq_count - first(mean_seq_count)) / first(mean_seq_count) * 100,
    label = ifelse(perc_change == 0,
                   "Baseline",
                   sprintf("%+.0f%%", perc_change))
  )

# 2. Compute completeness per depth for unique sequences

brz_mam_primer_completeness_depth_unique <- brz_mam_completeness_unique %>%
  select(!c(binomial, presence)) %>%
  group_by(region, primer) %>%
  summarize(
    ">=1"  = sum(nseq >= 1)  / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100,
    ">=2"  = sum(nseq >= 2)  / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100,
    ">=5"  = sum(nseq >= 5)  / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100,
    ">=10" = sum(nseq >= 10) / length(brz_mam_synonyms) * 100
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(cols = c(">=1", ">=2", ">=5", ">=10"),
                      names_to = "nseqs",
                      values_to = "seq_count") %>%
  mutate(nseqs = factor(nseqs, levels = c(">=1", ">=2", ">=5", ">=10")))

mean_by_threshold_unique <- brz_mam_primer_completeness_depth_unique %>%
  group_by(nseqs) %>%
  summarize(mean_seq_count = mean(seq_count, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(
    perc_change = (mean_seq_count - first(mean_seq_count)) / first(mean_seq_count) * 100,
    label = ifelse(perc_change == 0,
                   "Baseline",
                   sprintf("%+.0f%%", perc_change))
  )

```

**Plot the data:**

```{r}

# 3. Plot function 

primer_colors <- c(
  "12S" = "#68a898",
  "16S" = "#b62c25",
  "COI" = "#f6b332",
  "Cytb" = "#2965a2"
)

make_depth_plot <- function(data, summary_df, title) {
  
  ggplot(data, aes(x = nseqs, y = seq_count, color = region, fill = region, group = primer)) +
    
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 0.4) +
    
    geom_smooth(
      aes(group = 1),
      color = "black",
      se = FALSE,
      linewidth = 1.5,
      linetype = "solid",
      method = "loess",
      span = 0.8
    ) +
    
    geom_point(
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      data = summary_df,
      aes(x = nseqs, y = mean_seq_count),
      shape = 21, size = 4, fill = "white", color = "black", stroke = 1.2
    ) +
    
    geom_text(
      inherit.aes = FALSE,
      data = summary_df,
      aes(x = nseqs, y = 100, label = label),
      vjust = 0, size = 5, fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    
    scale_color_manual(values = primer_colors) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = primer_colors) +
    
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = c(0.05, 0.05)) +
    
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Species with barcode (%)") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, color = "black", face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 18, color = "black"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 20),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.position = "none",
      plot.title = element_text(size = 30, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5)
    ) +
    ggtitle(title)
}

primer_coverage_per_depth_all    <- make_depth_plot(brz_mam_primer_completeness_depth_all,    mean_by_threshold,        "All sequences")

primer_coverage_per_depth_all

primer_coverage_per_depth_unique <- make_depth_plot(brz_mam_primer_completeness_depth_unique, mean_by_threshold_unique, "Unambiguous sequences")

primer_coverage_per_depth_unique
```

### 1.2.4. ***Mean database completeness per order***

Code for plotting Figure 1B.

**Prepare the data:**

```{r}

# 1. Mean completeness per clade — ALL

brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all <- 
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_all %>%
    select(primer, order, cumsum, n_species, region) %>%
    distinct() %>%
    group_by(primer, order) %>%
    summarise(
      cumsum = mean(cumsum),
      region = first(region),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(order) %>%
    mutate(mean_percentage = mean(cumsum)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(desc(mean_percentage))


# 2. Mean completeness per clade — UNIQUE

brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique <- 
  brz_mam_clade_primer_completeness_unique %>%
  select(primer, order, cumsum, n_species, region) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  group_by(primer, order) %>%
  summarise(
      cumsum = mean(cumsum),
      region = first(region),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  mutate(mean_percentage = mean(cumsum)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_percentage))


# 3. Set factor order (after arranging)

brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all$order <- factor(
  brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all$order,
  levels = unique(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all$order)
)

brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique$order <- factor(
  brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique$order,
  levels = unique(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique$order)
)


# 4. Summary statistics

mean_overall_percentage_all    <- mean(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all$mean_percentage)
sd_overall_percentage_all      <- sd(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all$mean_percentage)

mean_overall_percentage_unique <- mean(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique$mean_percentage)
sd_overall_percentage_unique   <- sd(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique$mean_percentage)
```

```{r}
# 1. Compute mean completeness values (overall)

library(forcats)

mean_overall_all <- mean(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all$cumsum, na.rm = TRUE)
mean_overall_unique <- mean(brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique$cumsum, na.rm = TRUE)


# 2. Prepare summary tables for plotting

# All sequences

brz_summary_all <- brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all %>%
  rename(order_col = order, cumsum_val = cumsum) %>%
  group_by(order_col) %>%
  summarise(mean_order = mean(cumsum_val, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(order_col = fct_reorder(order_col, mean_order))

# Unique sequences

brz_summary_unique <- brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique %>%
  rename(order_col = order, cumsum_val = cumsum) %>%
  group_by(order_col) %>%
  summarise(mean_order = mean(cumsum_val, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(order_col = fct_reorder(order_col, mean_order))


# 3. Plot mean completeness per clade (ALL sequences)

mean_coverage_per_taxon_all <- 
  brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all %>%
  rename(order_col = order, cumsum_val = cumsum) %>%
  mutate(order_col = fct_reorder(order_col, cumsum_val)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = order_col, y = cumsum_val)) +
  
  # Vertical lines showing deviation from global mean
  geom_segment(
    data = brz_summary_all,
    aes(x = order_col, xend = order_col,
```

### 1.2.5. ***Sequence ambiguity and divergence***

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=8, fig.dpi=600}
brz_mam_seq_sp_shared <-
```

***Mean distance in amplicon sequences between species per primer:***

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=8, fig.dpi=600}

# 1. Prepare the data

# Remove species without a sequence

brz_mam_sequences_clean <- na.omit(brz_mam_sequences_all)

# One representative sequence per species and primer: the medoid, i.e. the
# sequence with the smallest summed distance to all other sequences of the
# same species. This uses all sequences of a species without random sampling.
# Ties are resolved alphabetically, the result does not depend on the input order.

medoid_sequence <- function(seqs) {
  seqs <- sort(unique(seqs))
  if (length(seqs) == 1) return(seqs)
  dist <- as.matrix(pwalign::stringDist(Biostrings::DNAStringSet(seqs), method = "levenshtein"))
  seqs[which.min(rowSums(dist))]
}

brz_mam_seq_res <- brz_mam_sequences_clean %>%
  group_by(primer, region, binomial) %>%
  summarise(n_sequences = n_distinct(sequence),
            sequence    = medoid_sequence(sequence),
            .groups = "drop")

# 2. Mean distance of each species to all other species, per primer

brz_mam_seq_res <- brz_mam_seq_res %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  group_modify(function(d, key) {
    dist <- as.matrix(pwalign::stringDist(Biostrings::DNAStringSet(d$sequence), method = "levenshtein"))
    d$meandist <- rowSums(dist) / (nrow(dist) - 1)
    d
  }) %>%
  ungroup()

# Prepare additional variables

brz_mam_seq_res <- 
  
  brz_mam_seq_res %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  mutate(mean_meandist = mean(meandist)) %>%
  ungroup()%>%
  arrange(desc(mean_meandist))
  

mean_overall_dist <- mean(brz_mam_seq_res$meandist)
sd_overall_dist <- sd(brz_mam_seq_res$meandist)

brz_mam_seq_res$primer <- factor(brz_mam_seq_res$primer,
                                 levels = levels(brz_mam_seq_sp_shared$primer))

# Positions of the points, jittered to the left of each primer

set.seed(12345)
brz_mam_seq_res$point_x <- as.integer(brz_mam_seq_res$primer) - runif(nrow(brz_mam_seq_res), 0.05, 0.3)

# 3. Plot the data

brz_mam_distance_plot<-
  ggplot(brz_mam_seq_res, aes(x = as.integer(primer), 
                            y = meandist)) + 
  
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = -Inf, 
                xmax = +Inf,
                ymin = mean_overall_dist - sd_overall_dist,
                ymax= mean_overall_dist + sd_overall_dist), 
            color = "grey95",
            fill = "grey95", 
            alpha = 0.75)+
  
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_overall_dist, 
             linetype = "dashed", 
             linewidth = 0.5, 
             color = "grey30")+
  
  geom_polygon(data = half_violin_polygons(brz_mam_seq_res, "primer", "meandist"),
               aes(x = x, y = y, group = group, fill = region, color = region),
               alpha = 0.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +

  geom_point(aes(x = point_x, color = region),
             alpha = .1, size = .5) +
  
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#68a898", "#b62c25", "#f6b332", "#2965a2"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#68a898", "#b62c25", "#f6b332", "#2965a2"))+

  geom_segment(aes(x = as.integer(primer),
                   xend = as.integer(primer),
                   y= mean_meandist,
                   yend= mean_overall_dist),
               color="grey30",
               linewidth = 0.5) +
  
  stat_summary(geom = "point", fun = mean)+
  
  labs(title = "Mean Levenshtein distance (bp)")+
  
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0.5, nlevels(brz_mam_seq_res$primer) + 0.5),
                     expand = expansion(add = 0.1)) +

  coord_flip()+
  
  theme_bw() + 
  
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(color = NA, fill = "white"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.1, color = "grey75"),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", 
                              size = 12,
                              color = "black",

                              vjust = 0),
    plot.title.position = "plot",
    plot.caption.position = "plot",
    axis.title.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
    axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 16, color = "black"),
```

***Relationship between ambiguity and Levenshtein distance / amplicon length:***

Create Figure 1D.

```{r, fig.width=7, fig.height=7, dpi=600}

# 1. Prepare the data

# Ambiguity

ambig_summary <-
  brz_mam_seq_sp_shared %>%
  select(primer, percentage_shared_species, region) %>%
  distinct()

# Levenshtein distance

dist_summary <- 
  brz_mam_seq_res %>%
  select(primer, mean_meandist) %>%
  distinct()

# # Species per duplication

dup_summary <- brz_mam_seq_dupl %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  summarise(max_species_per_dup = max(n_species_shared, na.rm = TRUE))

# Mean barcode length

length_summary <- 
  brz_mam_sequences_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(sequence)) %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  summarize(mean_length = mean(nchar(sequence), na.rm = TRUE))

# Combine all summaries

primer_summary <- 
  ambig_summary %>%
  left_join(dist_summary, by = "primer") %>%
  left_join(length_summary, by = "primer")%>%
  left_join(dup_summary, by = "primer")

primer_summary <- primer_summary %>%
  mutate(divergence = (mean_meandist / mean_length) * 100)


# Compute Pearson correlation
cor_test <- cor.test(primer_summary$divergence, 
                     primer_summary$percentage_shared_species, 
                     method = "pearson")

# Prepare label text
cor_label <- paste0(
  "r = ", round(cor_test$estimate, 2),
  ", p = ", signif(cor_test$p.value, 3)
)

# 2. Plot the data

ambiguity_by_divergence <- 
  
  ggplot(primer_summary, aes(x = divergence, y = percentage_shared_species)) +
  geom_point(aes(fill = region), shape = 21, size = 5, color = "black") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = FALSE, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_text(aes(label = primer), vjust = -1, size = 4, fontface = "bold", 
            nudge_y = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#68a898", "#b62c25", "#f6b332", "#2965a2")) +
  labs(
    x = "Mean divergent sites per barcode (%)",
    y = "Species with ambiguous sequences (%)"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0.1, 0.1)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14, color = "black", face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 14, color = "black"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 16, color = "black"),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "transparent"),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 30),
    legend.position = "none"
  ) +
  # Add correlation
  annotate("text", x = 30, y = 30, label = cor_label, size = 6, fontface = "bold")

# 3. Save the plot

save_figure(ambiguity_by_divergence, "Fig1d_ambiguity_vs_divergence", width = 7, height = 7)
```

***Check the degree of ambiguity for each taxonomic clade-barcode combination:***

Code used to produce Figure 1E.

```{r, fig.height=7, fig.width=7, dpi = 600}

# 1. Prepare the data

# Identify ambiguous sequences (same sequence used by ≥2 species)

ambig_seqs <- brz_mam_sequences_all %>%
  left_join(brz_mam_taxonomy[, c("binomial", "order")], by = "binomial") %>%
  filter(!is.na(sequence)) %>%
  group_by(primer, sequence) %>%
  filter(n_distinct(binomial) > 1) %>%         # ambiguous sequences
  summarise(shared_species = list(unique(binomial)), .groups = "drop")

# Unnest and restore species + clade information

ambig_seqs_clade <- ambig_seqs %>%
  unnest(shared_species) %>%
  rename(binomial = shared_species) %>%
  left_join(brz_mam_taxonomy[, c("binomial", "order")], by = "binomial")

# Count ambiguous species per primer × clade

ambig_summary <- ambig_seqs_clade %>%
  group_by(primer, order) %>%
  summarise(
    n_ambig_species = n_distinct(binomial),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Count total species per clade

clade_sizes <- brz_mam_taxonomy %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  summarise(n_species_in_clade = n_distinct(binomial), .groups = "drop")

# Compute fraction ambiguous per primer × clade

ambig_fraction <- ambig_summary %>%
  left_join(clade_sizes, by = "order") %>%
  mutate(fraction_ambiguous = n_ambig_species / n_species_in_clade)

# Ensure all primer × clade combinations exist

all_primers <- unique(brz_mam_sequences_all$primer)
all_orders  <- unique(brz_mam_taxonomy$order)

ambig_fraction <- ambig_fraction %>%
  tidyr::complete(
    primer = all_primers,
    order = all_orders,
    fill = list(
      n_ambig_species = 0,
      fraction_ambiguous = 0
    )
  )

# Reorder factors for plotting

primer_means <- ambig_fraction %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  summarise(mean_fraction = mean(fraction_ambiguous, na.rm = TRUE))

clade_means <- ambig_fraction %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  summarise(mean_fraction = mean(fraction_ambiguous, na.rm = TRUE))

ambig_fraction <- ambig_fraction %>%
  mutate(
    primer = factor(primer, levels = rev(primer_means$primer[order(-primer_means$mean_fraction)])),
    order  = factor(order,  levels = clade_means$order[order(-clade_means$mean_fraction)])
  )


# 2. Plot the data

ambig_seq_per_primer_clade <- ggplot(ambig_fraction,
                                     aes(x = order, y = primer, fill = fraction_ambiguous * 100)) +
  
  geom_tile(color = "black") +
  
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "#440154FF",
    na.value = "grey90",
    limits = c(0, max(ambig_fraction$fraction_ambiguous, na.rm = TRUE) * 100)
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    data = filter(ambig_fraction, fraction_ambiguous > 0),
    aes(
      label = paste0(round(fraction_ambiguous * 100, 1), "%"),
      color = ifelse(
        fraction_ambiguous > max(ambig_fraction$fraction_ambiguous, na.rm = TRUE) / 2,
        "white", "black"
      )
    ),
    size = 4.5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  scale_color_identity() +
  labs(
    x = "Clade (Order)",
    y = "Primer",
    fill = "Fraction ambiguous (%)",
    title = "Percentage of Species with Ambiguous Barcodes"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold")
  )


# 3. Save the plot

save_figure(ambig_seq_per_primer_clade, "Fig1e_ambiguity_by_order", width = 7, height = 7)
```

***Sources of sequence ambiguity:***

Ambiguity can only be detected when both species that share a sequence have been sequenced. Differences in ambiguity between orders can therefore reflect real differences in how genetically similar species are, or differences in how well close relatives have been sequenced. We look at this in three ways, using all sequences of each species and the phylogenies from Part 1:

1.  **Under-detection:** we randomly remove sequenced species, keeping 20% to 100% of them (100 times each), and recount the proportion of the remaining species affected by ambiguity. If ambiguity is under-detected when fewer species are sequenced, this proportion drops as fewer species are kept.
2.  **Sequencing of the closest relative:** for each sequenced species, we check whether its sister species (its closest relative among the Brazilian mammals, based on the phylogenies averaged over the 100 trees) is also sequenced.
3.  **Divergence between sister species:** for sister species that are both sequenced, we take the smallest distance between any of their sequences (Levenshtein distance, as a percentage of sequence length), and compare it with the time since they split in the phylogeny.

Species grafted onto the phylogenies have an uncertain position, so we leave out species that were grafted, or whose sister species was grafted, from steps 2 and 3.

If low ambiguity in some orders is caused by missing relatives, we expect sister species to be sequenced less often in those orders. If it is caused by real differences between species, we expect larger distances between sister species, even when both are sequenced.

```{r, fig.width=14, fig.height=11}

# 1. Phylogenetic distances between Brazilian species, averaged over the 100 trees

tree_species <- sort(brz_mam_tree[[1]]$tip.label)

phylo_dist <- Reduce(`+`, lapply(brz_mam_tree, function(tree) {
  ape::cophenetic.phylo(tree)[tree_species, tree_species]
})) / length(brz_mam_tree)

diag(phylo_dist) <- NA

# 2. Species grafted onto the trees, whose position is uncertain

grafted_species <- brz_mam_tree[[1]]$graft_status %>%
  mutate(species = gsub("_", " ", species)) %>%
  filter(grepl("grafted", status)) %>%
  pull(species)

# 3. Sister species: the closest relative(s) of each species among the Brazilian species

sister_table <- tibble(
  binomial = tree_species,
  sisters  = lapply(tree_species, function(sp) {
    d <- phylo_dist[sp, ]
    names(d)[which(abs(d - min(d, na.rm = TRUE)) < 1e-6)]
  })
) %>%
  mutate(reliable = !(binomial %in% grafted_species) &
           !sapply(sisters, function(s) any(s %in% grafted_species))) %>%
  left_join(brz_mam_taxonomy[, c("binomial", "order")], by = "binomial")

message(sum(!sister_table$reliable), " of ", nrow(sister_table),
        " species left out because they or their sister species were grafted onto the trees")

# 4. All sequences per species and primer

seq_table <- brz_mam_sequences_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(sequence)) %>%
  distinct(primer, binomial, sequence)

seq_lookup <- split(seq_table$sequence, paste(seq_table$primer, seq_table$binomial, sep = "|"))

# 5. Sequencing of the closest relative: for each sequenced species and primer,
#    whether at least one of its sister species is also sequenced

sister_sampling <- seq_table %>%
  distinct(primer, binomial) %>%
  inner_join(filter(sister_table, reliable), by = "binomial") %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  mutate(sister_sequenced = sapply(sisters, function(s) any(s %in% binomial))) %>%
  ungroup()

# 6. Divergence between sister species: the smallest distance between any
#    sequence of one species and any sequence of its sister (% of sequence length)

min_sequence_distance <- function(seqs_a, seqs_b) {
  dist <- as.matrix(pwalign::stringDist(Biostrings::DNAStringSet(c(seqs_a, seqs_b)),
                                        method = "levenshtein"))
  dist <- dist[seq_along(seqs_a), length(seqs_a) + seq_along(seqs_b), drop = FALSE]
  seq_length <- outer(nchar(seqs_a), nchar(seqs_b), "+") / 2
  min(dist / seq_length) * 100
}

sister_pairs <- sister_sampling %>%
  filter(sister_sequenced) %>%
  select(primer, binomial, order, sisters) %>%
  tidyr::unnest_longer(sisters, values_to = "sister") %>%
  filter(paste(primer, sister, sep = "|") %in% names(seq_lookup)) %>%
  mutate(pair = ifelse(binomial < sister,
                       paste(binomial, sister, sep = " | "),
                       paste(sister, binomial, sep = " | "))) %>%
  distinct(primer, pair, .keep_all = TRUE)

sister_pairs$distance <- mapply(function(p, a, b) {
  min_sequence_distance(seq_lookup[[paste(p, a, sep = "|")]],
                        seq_lookup[[paste(p, b, sep = "|")]])
}, sister_pairs$primer, sister_pairs$binomial, sister_pairs$sister)

sister_pairs$divergence_time <- phylo_dist[cbind(sister_pairs$binomial, sister_pairs$sister)] / 2

# One value per sister pair: the median distance across primers, and whether
# the pair shares an identical sequence for at least one primer

pair_summary <- sister_pairs %>%
  group_by(pair, order) %>%
  summarise(median_distance = median(distance),
            ambiguous       = any(distance == 0),
            n_primers       = n(),
            divergence_time = first(divergence_time),
            .groups = "drop")

save_table(pair_summary, "sister_pair_distances", type = "additional")

# 7. Under-detection: randomly keep 20-100% of the sequenced species per primer
#    and recount the proportion of the kept species affected by ambiguity

ambiguous_species <- function(tab) {
  counts <- table(tab$sequence)
  unique(tab$binomial[tab$sequence %in% names(counts)[counts > 1]])
}

order_lookup  <- setNames(brz_mam_taxonomy$order, brz_mam_taxonomy$binomial)
seq_by_primer <- split(seq_table[, c("binomial", "sequence")], seq_table$primer)
retained      <- c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1)
n_reps        <- 100

set.seed(12345)

subsampling <- bind_rows(lapply(retained, function(f) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(if (f == 1) 1 else n_reps), function(r) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(seq_by_primer), function(p) {
      tab     <- seq_by_primer[[p]]
      species <- unique(tab$binomial)
      kept    <- sample(species, round(f * length(species)))
      amb     <- ambiguous_species(tab[tab$binomial %in% kept, ])
      tibble(retained = f, rep = r, primer = p,
             order = unname(order_lookup[kept]), ambiguous = kept %in% amb)
    }))
  }))
}))

subsampling_summary <- subsampling %>%
  group_by(order, retained, rep) %>%
  summarise(fraction_ambiguous = mean(ambiguous), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(order, retained) %>%
  summarise(median = median(fraction_ambiguous) * 100,
            lower  = quantile(fraction_ambiguous, 0.025) * 100,
            upper  = quantile(fraction_ambiguous, 0.975) * 100,
            .groups = "drop")

# 8. Summary per order (orders with at least 10 species)

main_orders <- brz_mam_taxonomy %>%
  count(order) %>%
  filter(n >= 10) %>%
  pull(order)

ambiguity_sources_by_order <- subsampling_summary %>%
  filter(retained %in% c(0.2, 1)) %>%
  select(order, retained, median) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = retained, values_from = median,
                     names_prefix = "percent_ambiguous_kept_") %>%
  rename(percent_ambiguous = percent_ambiguous_kept_1,
         percent_ambiguous_at_20 = percent_ambiguous_kept_0.2) %>%
  left_join(sister_sampling %>%
              group_by(order) %>%
              summarise(percent_sister_sequenced = mean(sister_sequenced) * 100,
                        n_species_with_reliable_sister = n_distinct(binomial),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "order") %>%
  left_join(pair_summary %>%
              group_by(order) %>%
              summarise(n_sister_pairs           = n(),
                        median_sister_distance   = median(median_distance),
                        percent_pairs_ambiguous  = mean(ambiguous) * 100,
                        median_divergence_time   = median(divergence_time),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "order") %>%
  filter(order %in% main_orders) %>%
  arrange(desc(percent_ambiguous))

ambiguity_sources_by_order

save_table(ambiguity_sources_by_order, "ambiguity_sources_by_order", type = "additional")

# 9. Plot

order_levels <- ambiguity_sources_by_order$order

order_colors <- c(
  "Didelphimorphia" = "#92ad88",
  "Cingulata"       = "#73968d",
  "Pilosa"          = "#e8ccad",
  "Primates"        = "#e3a88c",
  "Rodentia"        = "#cc9ea5",
  "Artiodactyla"    = "#9ba3c8",
  "Carnivora"       = "#94a7b8",
  "Chiroptera"      = "#80a0a6"
)

theme_ambiguity <- theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text  = element_text(colour = "black"),
        axis.title = element_text(colour = "black"),
        legend.title = element_blank())

# a) Proportion affected by ambiguity when fewer species are sequenced

p_subsampling <- subsampling_summary %>%
  filter(order %in% main_orders) %>%
  mutate(order = factor(order, levels = order_levels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = retained * 100, y = median, colour = order, fill = order)) +

# b) Sequencing of the closest relative

p_sister_sampling <- sister_sampling %>%
  filter(order %in% main_orders) %>%
  group_by(primer, order) %>%
  summarise(percent_sister_sequenced = mean(sister_sequenced) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%

  theme_ambiguity +

# c) Divergence between sister species

p_sister_distance <- pair_summary %>%
  filter(order %in% main_orders) %>%
  mutate(order = factor(order, levels = order_levels)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = order, y = median_distance, fill = order)) +

# d) Sequence distance against time since the split

p_distance_time <- pair_summary %>%
  filter(order %in% main_orders) %>%
  mutate(order = factor(order, levels = order_levels),
         ambiguous = ifelse(ambiguous, "Shared sequence", "No shared sequence")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = divergence_time, y = median_distance, colour = order, shape = ambiguous)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, alpha = 0.8) +

  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Shared sequence" = 17, "No shared sequence" = 16)) +
  labs(x = "Time since split from sister species (million years, log scale)",
       y = "Sequence distance between sister species (%)") +
  guides(colour = "none") +
  theme_ambiguity

ambiguity_sources_plot <- (p_subsampling | p_sister_sampling) /
  (p_sister_distance | p_distance_time) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  plot_annotation(tag_levels = "a")

ambiguity_sources_plot

save_figure(ambiguity_sources_plot, "FigS14_sources_of_sequence_ambiguity",
            width = 14, height = 11, type = "supplementary")

# Values used in the interpretation below

n_excluded <- sum(!sister_table$reliable)

val <- function(ord, col) {
  round(ambiguity_sources_by_order[[col]][ambiguity_sources_by_order$order == ord], 1)
}

val_range <- function(ords, col) {
  x <- round(range(ambiguity_sources_by_order[[col]][ambiguity_sources_by_order$order %in% ords]), 1)
  paste0(x[1], "–", x[2])
}

rm(tree_species, phylo_dist, grafted_species, sister_table, seq_table, seq_lookup,
   sister_sampling, min_sequence_distance, sister_pairs, pair_summary, ambiguous_species,
   order_lookup, seq_by_primer, retained, n_reps, subsampling, subsampling_summary,
   main_orders, order_levels, order_colors, theme_ambiguity, p_subsampling,
   p_sister_sampling, p_sister_distance, p_distance_time, ambiguity_sources_plot,
   brz_mam_tree)

```

The table `ambiguity_sources_by_order` summarises the three analyses per order. Points in panels b and c show individual primers and sister pairs, respectively.

> **Interpretation**: When we keep fewer of the sequenced species, the proportion affected by ambiguity drops in every order (panel A). In primates, it falls from `r val("Primates", "percent_ambiguous")`% with all sequenced species to `r val("Primates", "percent_ambiguous_at_20")`% with 20% of them, and in rodents from `r val("Rodentia", "percent_ambiguous")`% to `r val("Rodentia", "percent_ambiguous_at_20")`%. Ambiguity is therefore under-detected when fewer species are sequenced, and the current values reported in the main text are likely underestimates.
>
> Sister species are sequenced less often in rodents, bats and didelphid marsupials (`r val_range(c("Rodentia", "Chiroptera", "Didelphimorphia"), "percent_sister_sequenced")`% of sequenced species have a sequenced sister species) than in carnivores, artiodactylans, sloths and anteaters, and armadillos (`r val_range(c("Carnivora", "Artiodactyla", "Pilosa", "Cingulata"), "percent_sister_sequenced")`%; panel B). Primates are in between (`r val("Primates", "percent_sister_sequenced")`%), yet have by far the most ambiguity, so missing relatives do not explain the differences between orders on their own.
>
> When both sister species are sequenced, their sequences differ much less in primates and artiodactylans (median `r val("Primates", "median_sister_distance")`% and `r val("Artiodactyla", "median_sister_distance")`%) than in rodents, bats, carnivores and didelphid marsupials (`r val_range(c("Rodentia", "Chiroptera", "Carnivora", "Didelphimorphia"), "median_sister_distance")`%; panel C). This also holds for sister species that split at similar times (panel D). High ambiguity in primates and artiodactylans therefore reflects closely related species with very similar mitochondrial sequences, while lower ambiguity in rodents, bats and didelphid marsupials reflects both greater differences between species and incomplete sequencing of close relatives.
>
> `r n_excluded` of 731 species were left out of panels B–D because they or their sister species were grafted onto the phylogenies. Grafted species are often recently described or split, which are the species most likely to share sequences, so panels B–D may underestimate ambiguity. Artiodactyla, Pilosa and Cingulata have few sister pairs, so their values in panels C and D are indicative only.

```{r}

rm(n_excluded, val, val_range, ambiguity_sources_by_order)

```

### 1.2.7. ***Statistics reported in the main text***

Values reported in the Results that cannot be read directly from Figures 1 and 2. All values are calculated from the species-level completeness tables and sequences, so they do not depend on the plotting objects above.

```{r}

# 1. Completeness per primer, for all and unambiguous sequences

completeness_by_primer <- brz_mam_completeness_all %>%
  group_by(region, primer) %>%
  summarise(completeness_all = mean(presence) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(brz_mam_completeness_unique %>%
              group_by(primer) %>%
              summarise(completeness_unambiguous = mean(presence) * 100, .groups = "drop"),
            by = "primer") %>%
  arrange(desc(completeness_all))

completeness_by_primer

cat("Median completeness across primers:",
    round(median(completeness_by_primer$completeness_all), 1), "% (all),",
    round(median(completeness_by_primer$completeness_unambiguous), 1), "% (unambiguous)\n")

# 2. Completeness per primer and order, and mean per order across primers

order_size <- brz_mam_taxonomy %>%
  count(order, name = "n_species")

completeness_by_primer_order <- brz_mam_completeness_all %>%
  left_join(brz_mam_taxonomy[, c("binomial", "order")], by = "binomial") %>%
  group_by(order, region, primer) %>%
  summarise(completeness_all = mean(presence) * 100, .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(brz_mam_completeness_unique %>%
              left_join(brz_mam_taxonomy[, c("binomial", "order")], by = "binomial") %>%
              group_by(order, primer) %>%
              summarise(completeness_unambiguous = mean(presence) * 100, .groups = "drop"),
            by = c("order", "primer"))

save_table(completeness_by_primer_order, "completeness_by_primer_and_order", type = "additional")

# Loss of effective coverage: difference between all and unambiguous sequences,
# in percentage points and relative to the completeness for all sequences

completeness_by_order <- completeness_by_primer_order %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  summarise(mean_completeness_all         = mean(completeness_all),
            mean_completeness_unambiguous = mean(completeness_unambiguous),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(loss_percentage_points = mean_completeness_all - mean_completeness_unambiguous,
         loss_relative_percent  = loss_percentage_points / mean_completeness_all * 100) %>%
  left_join(order_size, by = "order") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_completeness_all))

completeness_by_order

cat("Overall mean completeness across orders:",
    round(mean(completeness_by_order$mean_completeness_all), 1), "% (all),",
    round(mean(completeness_by_order$mean_completeness_unambiguous), 1), "% (unambiguous)\n")

# 3. Sequence ambiguity: species with at least one sequence shared with another species

ambiguity_by_species <- brz_mam_sequences_all %>%
  filter(!is.na(sequence)) %>%
  distinct(region, primer, binomial, sequence) %>%
  group_by(primer, sequence) %>%
  mutate(shared = n_distinct(binomial) > 1) %>%
  group_by(region, primer, binomial) %>%
  summarise(ambiguous = any(shared), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(brz_mam_taxonomy[, c("binomial", "order")], by = "binomial")

# Per primer, as a percentage of species with at least one sequence

ambiguity_by_primer <- ambiguity_by_species %>%
  group_by(region, primer) %>%
  summarise(n_sequenced = n(),
            n_ambiguous = sum(ambiguous),
            percent_ambiguous = n_ambiguous / n_sequenced * 100,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(percent_ambiguous))

ambiguity_by_primer

cat("Species affected by ambiguity per primer:",
    round(min(ambiguity_by_primer$percent_ambiguous), 1), "-",
    round(max(ambiguity_by_primer$percent_ambiguous), 1), "% of sequenced species\n")

# Per primer and order, as a percentage of sequenced species and of all species in the order

ambiguity_by_primer_order <- ambiguity_by_species %>%
  group_by(order, region, primer) %>%
  summarise(n_sequenced = n(),
            n_ambiguous = sum(ambiguous),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(order_size, by = "order") %>%
  mutate(percent_of_sequenced = n_ambiguous / n_sequenced * 100,
         percent_of_all       = n_ambiguous / n_species * 100)

save_table(ambiguity_by_primer_order, "ambiguity_by_primer_and_order", type = "additional")

ambiguity_max_by_order <- ambiguity_by_primer_order %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  summarise(max_percent_of_sequenced = max(percent_of_sequenced),
            max_percent_of_all       = max(percent_of_all),
            primer_at_max            = primer[which.max(percent_of_all)],
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(max_percent_of_all))

ambiguity_max_by_order

# 4. Haplotypic depth: percentage of species with at least 1, 2, 5 and 10
#    distinct sequences, per primer and summarised across primers

depth_thresholds <- c(1, 2, 5, 10)

depth_by_primer <- bind_rows(
  brz_mam_completeness_all %>% mutate(sequences = "all"),
  brz_mam_completeness_unique %>% mutate(sequences = "unambiguous")
) %>%
  tidyr::crossing(threshold = depth_thresholds) %>%
  group_by(sequences, primer, threshold) %>%
  summarise(percent_species = mean(nseq >= threshold) * 100, .groups = "drop")

depth_summary <- depth_by_primer %>%
  group_by(sequences, threshold) %>%
  summarise(mean_percent   = mean(percent_species),
            median_percent = median(percent_species),
            min_percent    = min(percent_species),
            max_percent    = max(percent_species),
            .groups = "drop")

depth_summary

# Species with fewer than two sequences, averaged across primers

cat("Species with fewer than two sequences (mean across primers):",
    round(100 - depth_summary$mean_percent[depth_summary$sequences == "all" & depth_summary$threshold == 2], 1),
    "%\n")

rm(order_size, ambiguity_by_species, depth_thresholds, depth_by_primer)
```

The full tables per primer and order are saved in `output/tables/additional/` (`completeness_by_primer_and_order`, `ambiguity_by_primer_and_order`). "Loss of effective coverage" is given both in percentage points (`loss_percentage_points`) and relative to the completeness for all sequences (`loss_relative_percent`); the Results report percentage points.

## 1.3. Explore database complementarity

### 1.3.1. ***Completeness of primer pairs, overall and per order***

Code used to produce Figure 2B.

**Prepare the data:**

```{r}

# 1. Step 1: Add "All" class and merge clade-specific orders

#    - Create a copy of all sequences
#    - Add a pseudo-clade "All"
#    - Merge with taxonomy to include real orders for each species

brz_mam_sequences_class <- brz_mam_sequences_all
brz_mam_sequences_class$order <- c("All")

brz_mam_sequences_class <- rbind(
  brz_mam_sequences_class, 
  merge(brz_mam_sequences_all, brz_mam_taxonomy[, c("binomial", "order")], by = "binomial")
)

# 2. Step 2: Separate sequences per clade and handle duplicates

#    - For each clade, calculate number of sequences per primer per species (nseq_all)
#    - Identify sequences shared among multiple species and set them as NA
#    - Calculate number of unique sequences per primer per species (nseq_unique)

orders <- unique(brz_mam_sequences_class$order)
brz_mam_sequences_class_list <- vector("list", length(orders))

for (i in 1:length(orders)) {
  brz_mam_sequences_class_list[[i]] <- brz_mam_sequences_class[brz_mam_sequences_class$order == orders[i], ] %>%
    
    group_by(primer, binomial) %>%
    mutate(nseq_all = n_distinct(sequence, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    group_by(primer, sequence) %>%
    mutate(sequence = ifelse(n_distinct(binomial) > 1, NA, sequence)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    
    group_by(primer, binomial) %>%
    mutate(nseq_unique = n_distinct(sequence, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    select(!sequence) %>%
    unique()
}

names(brz_mam_sequences_class_list) <- orders

# 3. Step 3: Pivot wider to create binary matrices for primers per species

#    - For all sequences (nseq_all) and unique sequences (nseq_unique)
#    - Convert counts to logical TRUE/FALSE (presence/absence)

brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_class_list))
brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_class_list))

for (i in 1:length(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list)) {
  
  # Pivot all sequences
  brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]] <- brz_mam_sequences_class_list[[i]] %>%
    select(binomial, primer, nseq_all) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = primer, values_from = nseq_all)
  
  brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]][sapply(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]], is.numeric)] <- 
    lapply(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]][sapply(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]], is.numeric)], function(x) x > 0)
  
  # Pivot unique sequences
  brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]] <- brz_mam_sequences_class_list[[i]] %>%
    select(binomial, primer, nseq_unique) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = primer, values_from = nseq_unique)
  
  brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]][sapply(brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]], is.numeric)] <- 
    lapply(brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]][sapply(brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]], is.numeric)], function(x) x > 0)
}

# 4. Step 4: Generate all unique pairs of primers for pairwise comparisons

primer_pairs <- as.data.frame(t(combn(unique(brz_mam_sequences_all$primer), 2)))
colnames(primer_pairs) <- c("primer1", "primer2")

# 5. Step 5: Calculate individual primer performance

#    - % of species covered by each primer for all sequences and unique sequences

primer_performance <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list))

for (i in 1:length(primer_performance)) {
  primer_performance[[i]] <- data.frame(
    primer = toupper(colnames(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]][, 2:ncol(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]])])),
    performance_all = apply(
      brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]][, 2:ncol(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]])], 
      2, 
      function(x) (sum(x)/length(unique(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]]$binomial))*100)
    ),
    performance_unique = apply(
      brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]][, 2:ncol(brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]])], 
      2, 
      function(x) (sum(x)/length(unique(brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]]$binomial))*100)
    )
  )
}

# 6. Step 6: Compute pairwise performance between primers

#    - For each primer pair, determine species covered by either primer

brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list))
brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list))

for (i in 1:length(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all)) {
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]] <- vector("list")
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]] <- vector("list")
  
  for (j in 1:nrow(primer_pairs)) {
    
    primer1 <- as.character(primer_pairs[j, "primer1"][[1]])
    primer2 <- as.character(primer_pairs[j, "primer2"][[1]])
    
    # All sequences
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]][[j]] <- brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]] %>%
      mutate(
        seq_both = .data[[primer1]] | .data[[primer2]],
        primer_comb = toupper(paste0(primer1, " - ", primer2)),
        type = "all"
      ) %>%
      select(binomial, seq_both, primer_comb, type)
    
    # Unique sequences
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]][[j]] <- brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]] %>%
      mutate(
        seq_both = .data[[primer1]] | .data[[primer2]],
        primer_comb = toupper(paste0(primer1, " - ", primer2)),
        type = "unique"
      ) %>%
      select(binomial, seq_both, primer_comb, type)
    
  }
}

# 7. Step 7: Combine pairwise lists and calculate % species covered

for (i in 1:length(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all)) {
  
  # All sequences
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]] <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]]) %>%
    group_by(primer_comb) %>%
    summarize(n_species_all = sum(seq_both), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(perc_species_all = n_species_all / length(unique(brz_mam_sequences_all_class_list[[i]]$binomial)) * 100)
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]] <- transform(
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]],
    primer1 = sapply(strsplit(as.character(primer_comb), " - "), `[`, 1),
    primer2 = sapply(strsplit(as.character(primer_comb), " - "), `[`, 2)
  )
  
  # Unique sequences
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]] <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]]) %>%
    group_by(primer_comb) %>%
    summarize(n_species_unique = sum(seq_both), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(perc_species_unique = n_species_unique / length(unique(brz_mam_sequences_unique_class_list[[i]]$binomial)) * 100)
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]] <- transform(
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]],
    primer1 = sapply(strsplit(as.character(primer_comb), " - "), `[`, 1),
    primer2 = sapply(strsplit(as.character(primer_comb), " - "), `[`, 2)
  )
}

# 8. Step 8: Get max individual primer performance for each pair

get_max_performance <- function(primer1, primer2, performance_df, col) {
  perf1 <- performance_df[performance_df$primer == primer1, col]
  perf2 <- performance_df[performance_df$primer == primer2, col]
  return(max(perf1, perf2))
}

for (i in 1:length(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all)) {
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]]$max_ind_performance_all <- mapply(
    get_max_performance, 
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]]$primer1,
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]]$primer2,
    MoreArgs = list(performance_df = primer_performance[[i]], col = 2)
  )
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]]$max_ind_performance_unique <- mapply(
    get_max_performance,
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]]$primer1,
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]]$primer2,
    MoreArgs = list(performance_df = primer_performance[[i]], col = 3)
  )
}

# 9. Step 9: Combine all and compute primer gain

#    - Primer gain = combined pair performance minus max individual primer performance

brz_mam_multi_primer_clade <- vector("list", length(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all))

for (i in 1:length(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade)) {
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]] <- merge(
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]][ , !(names(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_all[[i]]) %in% c("primer1","primer2"))],
    brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]][ , !(names(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade_unique[[i]]) %in% c("primer1","primer2"))],
    by = "primer_comb"
  )
  
  # Split primer_comb into primer1 and primer2 as factors
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer1 <- sapply(strsplit(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer_comb, " - "), `[`, 1)
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer2 <- sapply(strsplit(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer_comb, " - "), `[`, 2)
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer1 <- factor(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer1,
                                                    levels = names(table(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer1))[order(table(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer1))])
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer2 <- factor(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer2,
                                                    levels = names(table(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer2))[order(table(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$primer2))])
  
  # Compute primer gain
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]] <- brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]] %>%
    mutate(
      primer_gain_all = perc_species_all - max_ind_performance_all,
      primer_gain_unique = perc_species_unique - max_ind_performance_unique
    )
  
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[[i]]$order <- orders[i]
}

# Combine all clades into a single data.table

brz_mam_multi_primer_clade <- data.table::rbindlist(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade)

```

**Statistics reported in the main text: complementarity**

Values reported in the Results that cannot be read directly from Figure 2B. Pairs are classed as cross-locus (primers from different mitochondrial regions) or within-locus (same region). The gain is the difference between the completeness of the pair and the completeness of the better of its two primers.

```{r}

# 1. Region of each primer

primer_region <- brz_mam_completeness_all %>%
  distinct(primer, region) %>%
  mutate(primer = toupper(primer))

# 2. Pair completeness and gain, with pair type

pair_stats <- as.data.frame(brz_mam_multi_primer_clade) %>%
  mutate(primer1 = as.character(primer1),
         primer2 = as.character(primer2)) %>%
  left_join(rename(primer_region, primer1 = primer, region1 = region), by = "primer1") %>%
  left_join(rename(primer_region, primer2 = primer, region2 = region), by = "primer2") %>%
  mutate(pair_type = ifelse(region1 == region2, "within-locus", "cross-locus"))

# 3. Summary across all species, per pair type

pair_summary_all_species <- pair_stats %>%
  filter(order == "All") %>%
  group_by(pair_type) %>%
  summarise(
    n_pairs                          = n(),
    median_completeness_all          = median(perc_species_all),
    q1_completeness_all              = quantile(perc_species_all, 0.25),
    q3_completeness_all              = quantile(perc_species_all, 0.75),
    median_gain_all                  = median(primer_gain_all),
    median_completeness_unambiguous  = median(perc_species_unique),
    q1_completeness_unambiguous      = quantile(perc_species_unique, 0.25),
    q3_completeness_unambiguous      = quantile(perc_species_unique, 0.75),
    median_gain_unambiguous          = median(primer_gain_unique),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pair_summary_all_species

# Table S1: median completeness and gain of cross-locus and within-locus pairs

save_table(
  pair_summary_all_species %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric) & !n_pairs, ~ round(.x, 1))),
  "TableS1_cross_vs_within_locus_pairs",
  type = "supplementary"
)

# 4. Best pair across all species, with the gain in species

best_pair_all_species <- pair_stats %>%
  filter(order == "All") %>%
  arrange(desc(perc_species_all)) %>%
  select(primer_comb, pair_type, n_species_all, perc_species_all, primer_gain_all,
         n_species_unique, perc_species_unique, primer_gain_unique) %>%
  head(5)

best_pair_all_species

# 5. Best pair per order, and the completeness of the overall best pair in each order

overall_best_pair <- best_pair_all_species$primer_comb[1]

best_pair_by_order <- pair_stats %>%
  filter(order != "All") %>%
  group_by(order) %>%
  summarise(
    best_pair                    = primer_comb[which.max(perc_species_all)],
    best_pair_completeness       = max(perc_species_all),
    overall_best_pair_completeness = perc_species_all[primer_comb == overall_best_pair],
    difference                   = best_pair_completeness - overall_best_pair_completeness,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(difference))

best_pair_by_order

save_table(best_pair_by_order, "best_primer_pair_by_order", type = "additional")

# 6. Range of single-primer completeness across orders

single_primer_range <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(orders), function(i) {
  data.frame(order = orders[i], primer_performance[[i]])
})) %>%
  filter(order != "All")

cat("Single-primer completeness across orders:",
    round(min(single_primer_range$performance_all), 1), "-",
    round(max(single_primer_range$performance_all), 1), "%\n")

rm(primer_region, pair_stats, pair_summary_all_species, best_pair_all_species,
   overall_best_pair, best_pair_by_order, single_primer_range)

```

**Plot the data:**

```{r}

# 1. Step 1: Define Phylopic parameters for each order

#    - mirror: whether to flip the silhouette horizontally
#    - size_multiplier: scale factor for silhouette size

phylopic_params <- data.frame(
  order = names(phylopics), 
  mirror = c(TRUE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE), 
  size_multiplier = c(1.5, 2, 1.5, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 1.5, 0.8, 2, 1.5, 1.5)
)

# 2. Step 2: Initialize list to store heatmaps for each order

brz_mam_heatmap <- vector("list")

# 3. Step 3: Loop over each order to create heatmaps

for (i in 1:length(orders)) {
  
  # Filter data for the current order
  data <- brz_mam_multi_primer_clade[brz_mam_multi_primer_clade$order == orders[i], ]
  
  # 3A. Step 3a: Define thresholds for dynamic text color based on gain values
  
  #    - Text color = black if close to midpoint (within 10% of the range), else white
  
  ## For ALL sequences
  range_all <- max(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE) - min(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE)
  midpoint_all <- (max(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE) + min(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE)) / 2
  lower_all <- midpoint_all - 0.10 * range_all
  upper_all <- midpoint_all + 0.10 * range_all
  
  data$text_color_all <- ifelse(
    data$primer_gain_all >= lower_all & data$primer_gain_all <= upper_all,
    "black", "white"
  )
  
  ## For UNIQUE sequences
  range_unique <- max(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE) - min(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE)
  midpoint_unique <- (max(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE) + min(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE)) / 2
  lower_unique <- midpoint_unique - 0.10 * range_unique
  upper_unique <- midpoint_unique + 0.10 * range_unique
  
  data$text_color_unique <- ifelse(
    data$primer_gain_unique >= lower_unique & data$primer_gain_unique <= upper_unique,
    "black", "white"
  )
  
  # 3B. Step 3b: Heatmap for ALL sequences
  
  #    - Tile color = primer gain
  #    - Text = completeness (% species covered)
  
  brz_mam_heatmap_all <- ggplot(data, aes(primer1, primer2, fill = primer_gain_all)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = rev) +
    scico::scale_fill_scico(
      palette = "vik",
      limits = c(min(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE), max(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE)),
      name = "Gain over best primer (%)",
      breaks = seq(
        floor(min(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE)),
        ceiling(max(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE)),
        by = ceiling((ceiling(max(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE)) - floor(min(data$primer_gain_all, na.rm = TRUE))) / 6)
      ),
      na.value = "white"
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste0(round(perc_species_all, 1), "%"), color = text_color_all),
      size = 4.5,
      fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_color_identity() +  # literal color mapping
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_text(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.position = c(0.975, 0.05),
      legend.justification = c(1, 0),
      legend.direction = "horizontal",
      legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(vjust = 0.5),
      legend.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 5, b = 5, l = 5),
      plot.tag.position = c(0.25, 1.05)
    ) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))
  
  # Add Phylopic silhouettes if not the "All" category
  if (i > 1) {
    brz_mam_heatmap_all <- brz_mam_heatmap_all + 
      add_phylopic(
        img = phylopics[[orders[i]]], 
        x = "KOCHER", 
        y = "SARRI",  
        height = phylopic_params[phylopic_params$order == orders[i], ]$size_multiplier, 
        alpha = 0.8, 
        horizontal = phylopic_params[phylopic_params$order == orders[i], ]$mirror
      )
  }
  
  # 3C. Step 3c: Heatmap for UNIQUE sequences (unambiguous)
  
  #    - Same style as ALL, but text shows perc_species_unique
  
  brz_mam_heatmap_unique <- ggplot(data, aes(primer1, primer2, fill = primer_gain_unique)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = rev) +
    scico::scale_fill_scico(
      palette = "vik",
      limits = c(min(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE), max(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE)),
      name = "Gain over best primer (%)",
      breaks = seq(
        floor(min(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE)),
        ceiling(max(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE)),
        by = ceiling((ceiling(max(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE)) - floor(min(data$primer_gain_unique, na.rm = TRUE))) / 6)
      ),
      na.value = "white"
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = paste0(round(perc_species_unique, 1), "%"), color = text_color_unique),
      size = 4.5,
      fontface = "bold"
    ) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      legend.position = c(0.975, 0.05),
      legend.justification = c(1, 0),
      legend.direction = "horizontal",
      legend.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 8, face = "bold"),
      legend.text = element_text(vjust = 0.5),
      legend.margin = margin(6, 6, 6, 6),
      legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
      plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 5, b = 5, l = 5),
      plot.tag.position = c(0.05, 1.05)
    ) +
    guides(fill = guide_colorbar(title.position = "top", title.hjust = 0.5))
  
  # 3D. Step 3d: Combine ALL + UNIQUE heatmaps using patchwork
  
  brz_mam_heatmap[[i]] <- (brz_mam_heatmap_all | brz_mam_heatmap_unique) & 
    theme(plot.tag = element_text(face = 'bold', size = 20))
}
```

### 1.3.2. ***Ranking of primers and primer pairs across orders***

Weighted rank = primer rank \* (1 + gap in performance between primer / primer-pair and best-performing primer / primer-pair)

**Prepare the data:**

```{r}

# Step 1: Rank individual primers (all sequences)

brz_mam_primer_rank_all <-
  brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_all %>%
    group_by(order) %>%
    mutate(
      ranking = rank(desc(cumsum), ties.method = "min")
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(cumsum), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      best              = max(cumsum),
      diff_from_best    = best - cumsum,
      diff_fraction     = diff_from_best / best,
      weighted_ranking  = ranking * (1 + diff_fraction)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(primer) %>%
    mutate(
      mean_weighted_ranking = mean(weighted_ranking),
      sd_weighted_ranking   = sd(weighted_ranking)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(primer, region, mean_weighted_ranking, sd_weighted_ranking) %>%
    distinct()


# Step 2: Rank individual primers (unambiguous sequences only)

brz_mam_primer_rank_unique <-
  brz_mam_clade_mean_completeness_unique %>%
    group_by(order) %>%
    mutate(
      ranking = rank(desc(cumsum), ties.method = "min")
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(cumsum), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      best              = max(cumsum),
      diff_from_best    = best - cumsum,
      diff_fraction     = diff_from_best / best,
      weighted_ranking  = ranking * (1 + diff_fraction)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(primer) %>%
    mutate(
      mean_weighted_ranking = mean(weighted_ranking),
      sd_weighted_ranking   = sd(weighted_ranking)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(primer, region, mean_weighted_ranking, sd_weighted_ranking) %>%
    distinct()


# Step 3: Rank primer pairs (all sequences)
#   - Excludes pooled "All" order

brz_mam_primer_pair_rank_all <-
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade %>%
    filter(order != "All") %>%
    group_by(order) %>%
    mutate(
      ranking = rank(desc(perc_species_all), ties.method = "min")
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(perc_species_all), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      best              = max(perc_species_all),
      diff_from_best    = best - perc_species_all,
      diff_fraction     = diff_from_best / best,
      weighted_ranking  = ranking * (1 + diff_fraction)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(primer_comb) %>%
    mutate(
      mean_weighted_ranking = mean(weighted_ranking),
      sd_weighted_ranking   = sd(weighted_ranking)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(primer_comb, mean_weighted_ranking, sd_weighted_ranking) %>%
    distinct()


# Step 4: Rank primer pairs (unambiguous sequences only)
#   - Excludes pooled "All" order

brz_mam_primer_pair_rank_unique <-
  brz_mam_multi_primer_clade %>%
    filter(order != "All") %>%
    group_by(order) %>%
    mutate(
      ranking = rank(desc(perc_species_unique), ties.method = "min")
    ) %>%
    arrange(desc(perc_species_unique), .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(
      best              = max(perc_species_unique),
      diff_from_best    = best - perc_species_unique,
      diff_fraction     = diff_from_best / best,
      weighted_ranking  = ranking * (1 + diff_fraction)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    group_by(primer_comb) %>%
    mutate(
      mean_weighted_ranking = mean(weighted_ranking),
      sd_weighted_ranking   = sd(weighted_ranking)
    ) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(primer_comb, mean_weighted_ranking, sd_weighted_ranking) %>%
    distinct()
```
